useCase.summary: AI assistant that lists and files issues for a team in Linear.

verdict.headline: Linear needs no approval for this use case. Connect through Composio's managed OAuth2 with read and write scopes and you can list and file issues the same day.
verdict.startToday: There is no provider wait, so start with the Composio managed Linear connection (s2). If you later want your own branded OAuth app, register it in Linear at the same time (optional s5). Linear documents no review for that either.

composio.why: Composio has a managed Linear toolkit with OAUTH2 and the required scopes (read, write). Linear docs describe no review gate for OAuth apps, so the managed app is enough for production. Register your own app only if you need your own branding or workspace-level actor=app installs.

requirements.item: A Linear account that is a member of the target workspace and team, with permission to create issues
A Composio project and API key with the Linear toolkit enabled
Optional: a Linear OAuth2 app (client ID and secret) if you bring your own app instead of Composio's managed one

steps.title: Confirm Linear workspace access
steps.detail: Sign in to Linear and confirm you belong to the workspace and team where the assistant will file issues. Note the team key you will use when creating issues. Default user-mode OAuth needs no admin rights, and issues are created as the authorizing user.

steps.title: Authorize Linear through Composio managed OAuth2
steps.detail: In Composio, create a connection for the `linear` toolkit using the managed OAUTH2 auth config, requesting scopes `read` and `write`. Open the returned redirect link, pick the workspace on Linear's consent screen and approve. The connection becomes ACTIVE with no Linear app registration or review.

steps.title: Run LINEAR_LIST_LINEAR_ISSUES and LINEAR_CREATE_LINEAR_ISSUE
steps.detail: Execute both tools against the new connection. List issues with an explicit page size and a team filter, then create a test issue in a sandbox team and confirm it appears in Linear.

steps.title: Harden for production traffic
steps.detail: Set `first` explicitly and use filters when listing issues. Prefer webhooks over polling. Retry on HTTP 429 using the `Retry-After` header. Let Composio handle the 24-hour access token refresh.

steps.title: Optional: register your own Linear OAuth2 app and use it in Composio
steps.detail: Go to linear.app/settings/api/applications/new, create an OAuth2 application, and set the redirect callback URL to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Prefer a dedicated workspace to own the app so every admin has access. Choose private or public distribution. Copy the client ID and secret into a custom Composio auth config for `linear`, then reconnect. Skip this if the managed app is enough.

risks.title: actor=app installs need a workspace admin
risks.symptom: Installation with actor=app fails for non-admin users.
risks.fix: Use the default user actor, which creates issues as the authorizing user. If you want issues filed as the assistant itself, have a workspace admin do the install.

risks.title: Access tokens expire after 24 hours
risks.symptom: 401 errors a day after connecting if tokens are not refreshed.
risks.fix: Rely on Composio's managed refresh. If you run your own app, store the refresh token and refresh before expiry.

risks.title: Rate and complexity limits
risks.symptom: HTTP 429 with a RATELIMITED error code, or queries rejected for exceeding 10,000 complexity points.
risks.fix: Set `first` explicitly, filter issue lists, avoid polling, honour `Retry-After`, and ask Linear support for a temporary limit increase if needed.

risks.title: Changing client-credentials scopes revokes existing app tokens
risks.symptom: Existing app-actor tokens stop working after you request a token with different scopes.
risks.fix: Only relevant if you run your own app with client credentials. Keep the scope set fixed, and enable the client_credentials grant in the app settings if you see the unsupported-grant error.

risks.title: Integration directory listing is selective
risks.symptom: Linear may decline directory submissions from scripts or hobbyist apps.
risks.fix: Listing is optional and not needed for OAuth access. Submit only if you want discoverability in other workspaces, and email integrations@linear.app if unsure.

claims.text: Inferred: Linear's documentation describes no review or verification gate for OAuth apps, so no provider wait is expected for this use case. This rests on the absence of a documented gate.
Linear scopes include `read` (default), `write` and the narrower `issues:create`, which allows creating new issues and their attachments. `read` plus `write` covers listing and filing issues.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 authentication – Linear Developers
sources.quote: `issues:create` - Allows creating new issues and their attachments

verifier.note: The page lists read (default), write and issues:create with the stated description. Read plus write covering listing and filing issues is a reasonable reading of those scope descriptions.

claims.text: Integrations using actor=app cannot also request the `admin` scope.

sources.title: Getting Started – Linear Developers
sources.quote: Note that integrations using the `actor=app` mode are not able to also request `admin` scope.

verifier.note: The page states that integrations using actor=app cannot also request the admin scope.

claims.text: Installing an app with actor=app uses a workspace scope and requires workspace admin permissions.

sources.title: Getting Started – Linear Developers

claims.text: Linear access tokens are valid for 24 hours and must be refreshed.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 authentication – Linear Developers
sources.quote: The access token is valid for 24 hours and will need to be refreshed when it expires.

claims.text: A single query is capped at 10,000 complexity points and is rejected if it exceeds that.

sources.title: Rate limiting – Linear Developers
sources.quote: We also enforce a maximum complexity of a single query at any time to **10,000 points**. Your query will always get rejected if it exceeds that.

verifier.note: The page sets a 10,000-point maximum for a single query and says the query is always rejected above it.

claims.text: Linear discourages polling for updates and recommends webhooks. The default page size multiplies complexity, so set `first` explicitly and filter issue lists.

sources.title: Rate limiting – Linear Developers
sources.quote: One thing that we especially discourage is polling the API to fetch updates.

verifier.note: The page discourages polling, recommends webhooks, and says the default 50-record pagination multiplies complexity, so specify the record count and use filters.

openQuestions: Does Composio's managed Linear app have any workspace-level restrictions, or a rate-limit pool shared with other Composio tenants?
Is there any published review timeline or approval criteria for the Linear integration directory? None was found, and it is not required for OAuth access.
Does Linear impose any approval step on publicly distributed OAuth apps beyond the distribution setting? Docs show none, but this rests on absence of evidence.
